title: UX Design
blurb: User research, personas and journeys, interaction design, prototyping, usability testing and design systems.

quiz.question: Which interview question gives the most reliable insight?
options: Would you use a feature that does X?
Tell me about the last time you ordered dinner online
quiz.explanation: Ask about specific past behaviour, not hypothetical future intent.

quiz.question: Which method best reveals users' mental models for organising content?
quiz.explanation: Participants group and label content themselves.

quiz.question: About how many users per segment typically reveal most major usability problems in a flow?
quiz.explanation: Test iteratively with about 5 users per distinct group.

quiz.question: In a moderated usability test, a participant asks "What does this button do?" What do you say?
What is the WCAG AA minimum contrast for normal body text?
quiz.explanation: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text.

quiz.question: What do design tokens provide?
options: A single source of truth for design decisions (colour, spacing, type) shared across design and code
quiz.explanation: Change a token once and it propagates to all platforms.

quiz.question: Fitts's law implies that on mobile, primary actions should be…
options: Large and within easy thumb reach
quiz.explanation: Time to hit a target depends on its size and distance.

quiz.question: Which tool shows the end-to-end experience with emotions and pain points across stages?
quiz.explanation: Journey maps align teams around the whole experience.

problems.title: Fix a hidden feature
problems.prompt: Only 2% of orders use "schedule for later" despite strong demand in interviews. Plan your approach.
problems.solution: Check the funnel and discoverability in analytics, run a 5-user usability test with realistic tasks, identify issues (findability, wording), redesign with the control in the cart and plain language, retest, then ship behind a flag and measure adoption.
